captions.detailed: This 3D model is a parametric overhang test piece designed for evaluating 3D printer performance. It features a flat, circular cylindrical base disk from which a curved, rectangular-profile arch extends upwards and outwards. The arch resembles a section of a hollowed torus, starting at an angle from the base and terminating in a flat, vertical cross-section, forming a cantilevered overhang.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric 3D printer overhang test specimen in OpenSCAD. It should consist of a thin circular base plate and an angled, curved rectangular arch representing a partial torus section, with adjustable parameters for inner radius, width, depth, start angle, and base dimensions.
captions.factory: The script constructs the curved arch by translating a 2D square of dimensions [$depth, $width] by $innerRadius along the X-axis, and then applying a rotate_extrude() to form a torus. This torus is cropped using difference() with two large bounding cubes to leave only a specific angular sector. The resulting arch is rotated 90 degrees and translated to align with a simple cylinder primitive representing the base plate.
